title: The orchestrator runs where git is: ticfac in the container, the Workflow supervising
description:
PRINCIPLE: the orchestrator runs where a filesystem and git are. The Workflow supervises a run's LIFECYCLE and nothing else.

This is not a new architecture. It is the one docs/design/cloud-factory.md already specifies:

  "Orchestrator agent. A headless harness inside a named sandbox, running the exact loop
   from agent-runner.md ... When it dies, the Workflow boots a fresh orchestrator whose
   first instruction is the reconcile protocol."

  "The Run Workflow: owns one run's LIFECYCLE - boot the orchestrator sandbox, watch it,
   enforce wall-clock and cost budgets, retry a dead orchestrator, finalize."

EpicReconcilerWorkflow diverged from that by orchestrating INSIDE the isolate. Its own header
states the premise: "re-expressed for a host that cannot run tk". True of an isolate. Not true
of the sandbox the design doc puts the orchestrator in, and not true of the container this
factory already boots.

WHAT THE DIVERGENCE COST, measured on the 2026-09-20/21 gate runs. Every one of these is an
artifact of reimplementing git-over-HTTP in an isolate, not of the problem being solved:

  0h9  a plan pass read 1104 records one at a time and outlived its own lease
  8xd  ...so the tracker had to be read from a tarball instead, with a hand-written tar parser
  99f  writes silently went to the DEFAULT branch, because the contents API takes the ref in
       the query on a read and in the BODY on a write
  uim  the PAT's hourly budget was exhausted by passes re-reading the world over HTTP
  q35  a pass blocks for minutes, so the publish slot had to be kept alive by a heartbeat
  ijg  ...and a Workflow step is killed at 600s regardless
  991  a run inside one long step cannot report what it is doing

A local run has none of these. It clones, it uses worktrees, it runs tk, it pushes a branch and
opens a PR. The problems above do not exist there because the operations are git operations.

THE CHANGE, and it mostly deletes:

  - Put ticfac in the orchestrator image. The image already carries tk, git, Go, ripgrep and a
    real filesystem, and already has /usr/local/bin/ticks-orchestrator as the role entrypoint
    the Run Workflow starts and streams. It does NOT carry ticfac today (zero mentions in
    image/Dockerfile). That is the gap.
  - The Workflow boots the orchestrator container and supervises: budgets, liveness, retry a
    dead orchestrator, finalize. It does not orchestrate.
  - The orchestrator clones once per run and works on disk for the whole epic, pushing the
    epic branch and opening the PR at the end - which is what the operator asked for and what
    every comparable system does (actions/checkout, Codex cloud, Cursor and Sourcegraph all
    clone; only Dependabot reads files over the API, and only ~20 known manifests).
  - Deleted, not ported: epic-reconciler.ts, tracker-client.ts, git-contents.ts, tarball.ts,
    the contents-API write path, the publish-slot heartbeat. One reconciler, not two.

WHAT WE KEEP, and must not lose:
  - Determinism. EpicReconcilerWorkflow's real improvement over the design doc was replacing a
    MODEL-driven orchestration loop with code. Running ticfac in the container keeps that: it is
    the same deterministic reconciler, just hosted where git works. Do not regress to
    "an agent follows a skill loop".
  - Durable evidence and cold reconstruction. A dead orchestrator must be replaceable by a
    fresh one that re-derives from the remote - axiom 1, and the reason the local reconciler
    survives restarts today.
  - The publish slot / dispatch lease between CONCURRENT runs of one project. That arbitrates
    between runs and still matters; it is not what this change removes.
  - The PR + CI gate, and the merge staying a person's.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING (do not guess):
  1. Container lifetime. Can a Cloudflare container run for the length of an epic (hours), and
     what happens when it is evicted? The whole design rests on this and on cold reconstruction
     being real rather than assumed. Research is out.
  2. How do per-tick WORKER sandboxes relate to an orchestrator container - does the
     orchestrator spawn them via the Sandbox binding, and can it, from inside a container?
  3. What does the Workflow actually watch, and how does it know the orchestrator is alive
     without a keep-alive? (Operator, 2026-09-21: an architecture that relies on keep-alive is
     too brittle.) Durable evidence - branch heads moving - is the local answer.
  4. Cost and isolation: one long-lived orchestrator container per run, plus one sandbox per
     tick. Is that what the budget model assumes?

Supersedes the earlier framing of this epic, which took the isolate as given and only moved
work between steps. The step boundary is not the problem; the host is.
acceptance_criteria: A cloud epic run is driven by ticfac inside the orchestrator container against a real clone, pushing the epic branch and opening the PR at the end; the Workflow only boots, budgets, watches, retries and finalizes; a killed orchestrator is replaced by one that re-derives from the remote; and the TypeScript reconciler is deleted rather than maintained
